critical_code_review_comments: routes/wholesaler_orders.py is 1262 lines — exceeds the 700-line guideline. Split into wholesaler_orders.py + wholesaler_fulfillment.py + wholesaler_shipments.py. Each module is its own router included from server.py.

Route ordering hazard: the generic POST /shipments/{ship_id}/{action} catch-all shadowed /delay and /cancel until reordered. Same shape works fine for fulfillments because all actions there are declared explicitly. Consider replacing the catch-all with explicit /load, /start-transit, /deliver routes for clarity and to avoid future regressions.

Dispatch action performs N+1 writes: 1 shipment insert + N inventory finds/updates + N movement inserts + 1 fulfillment update + 1 order update — none wrapped in a transaction. If a mid-loop write fails, inventory and shipment state diverge. User has accepted this for demo per the request; flag for production hardening.

_decrement_stock_on_dispatch / _settle_in_transit_on_delivery / _adjust_reservation each do their own find_one+update_one. Coalesce into a single $inc update per product for atomicity and to halve round-trips.
_next_seq uses count_documents+1 — vulnerable to duplicate numbers under concurrency. Use a counters collection with $inc + upsert.

create_order tenant validation: `if len(products) != len(set(product_ids))` — if a product belongs to another tenant the catalog filter excludes it AND the dedup count comparison catches it, but the error 'not in tenant catalog' isn't strictly accurate for a duplicate-id-with-tenant-mismatch payload. Cosmetic.

modify_order: if has_approved is False and backorder_remainder is False, status becomes 'rejected' silently without a reject_reason — surfacing 'No quantities approved' is fine but the order field reject_reason is left empty and the UI may not have anything to show.

rca of the issue: Bug: POST /api/wholesaler/{wid}/shipments/{sid}/delay and /cancel both returned HTTP 400 'Unsupported action'. Root cause: FastAPI matches routes in registration order. The catch-all POST /shipments/{ship_id}/{action} was declared on line ~1138 BEFORE the explicit /delay (line ~1189) and /cancel (line ~1214). FastAPI matched the catch-all first with action='delay'|'cancel', which then fell through to the `if action not in _SHIP_ACTIONS: raise 400 'Unsupported action'` guard. Mitigation: moved the @router.post for the catch-all to the EOF via router.add_api_route(...). Verified by re-running pytest TestShipments::test_delay_then_cancel → PASS, full suite 30/30.
